system.name: Mint
system.one_liner: an agent-side tracing framework that parses spans into commonality patterns and variability parameters to capture all requests cheaply

components.name: Host
components.role: machine running the instrumented applications and Mint's agent-side components

components.name: Application Service
components.role: instrumented service handling ingress/egress traffic, containing tracepoints

components.name: Mint-agent
components.role: intercepts spans from tracepoints and forwards them for parsing

components.name: Pattern Library
components.role: stores common pattern parts extracted from spans

components.name: Params Buffer
components.role: stores variable parameter parts extracted from spans

components.name: Mint-collector
components.role: reports patterns, bloom filters, and selectively sampled parameters to the backend

components.name: Frontend
components.role: handles user queries and returns matched traces

components.name: Mint-backend
components.role: unified backend with a distributed trace storage engine that matches, rebuilds, and merges traces

components.name: Match
components.role: matches incoming pattern/bloom-filter data against stored traces

components.name: Rebuild Topo
components.role: reconstructs an approximate trace topology from matched patterns

components.name: Merge
components.role: merges pattern and parameter parts into an exact trace when sampled

flows.what: reported patterns, bloom filters, and sampled parameters
notification to report all parameters of a sampled trace

content.key_idea: Mint's implementation splits into per-host agents/collectors that separate common patterns from variable parameters, and a backend that matches, rebuilds, and selectively merges them into approximate or exact traces.
content.reading_order: Left block (Host: agent, pattern library, params buffer, collector) first, then rightward across colored arrows into the right block (Mint-backend: match, rebuild, merge) and up to Frontend/user.

Fig. 9 illustrates the implementation architecture of Mint.

summary: This figure shows Mint's implementation architecture, split into a Host region on the left and a Mint-backend region on the right. On each host, instrumented Application Services expose tracepoints; a Mint-agent extracts common pattern parts (stored in a Pattern Library) and variable parameter parts (stored in a Params Buffer) from each span, and a Mint-collector reports patterns and bloom filters continuously while selectively reporting sampled parameters. The Mint-backend, with a distributed trace storage engine, matches incoming pattern/bloom-filter data, rebuilds an approximate trace topology, and merges in parameters to produce an exact trace when the trace was sampled; a backend-to-host blue arrow notifies hosts to report all parameters of a sampled trace. A Frontend lets a user query traces. An in-figure legend defines the pattern/parameter/bloom-filter icons and the colored reporting arrows.
